subject: How to include SIR as as offset for forecasting period

messages.author: 5b42cf79c787b883
messages.subject: How to include SIR as as offset for forecasting period
parts:
Hi INLA group members,

I am working on a spatio-temporal model with type IV interaction to block level monthly cases data from 502 small areas (block) covering a period from Jan 2013 to Dec 2020 (96 months) along environment and climate covariates. I have fitted the model to the data covering Jan 2013 to Dec 2018 (training data set) and validated the model to the data (test data set) to the period from Jan 2019-Dec 2020. For your kind information while fitting and validating the model I have used the standardized incidence rate (SIR) as an offset in R-INLA. SIR for each month was calculated as a product of ‘r’ (ratio of total no. of cases to total population in a year) and population in a month.

Now I would like to apply the model to forecast the cases beyond the period of observations (i.e. Jan 2021 to Dec 2021). Since, I do not have the case data for the forecasting period, it would not be possible to calculate and include the SIR as an offset for this period. In this respect I seek the advice of the team on the following:

(i) can I make predictions for the out of sample period (Jan 2021-Dec 2021) without the offset?

(ii) can I use the monthly case data or the mean no. of cases for the previous year to calculate SIR (assuming the trend is same in 2021) and provide this as an offset.

(iii) any other suggestions?

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to include SIR as as offset for forecasting period
parts:
You might do both your suggestions, it is very case spesific what is a
reasonable approach to take in your application.

you might even do a 'smooth' model for SIR, or its log's, do a joint
model for the response and SIR, hence propagate the uncertainty in the
SIR into the predictions as well.

Best
H
